# dsh-opencode-routing
English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Русский

A DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) plugin that merges two earlier plugins
into one package: an **OpenCode ac

count pool with automatic A→B failover and quota routing**, plus a
**per-account / per-model usage d
ashboard**. Both live on a single Settings page, "OpenCode 账户与用量".
- **Client**: one `settings.section`, refreshed every 60 s; accounts can be added, edited, reordered

and probed;
model cards carry capability tags; both tables pan by dragging; the UI speaks 10 langua

ges (browser language wins).
- **Host**: two endpoints — `GET /opencode-usage.json` (usage, `?refres

h=1` forces a refresh) and
`GET|POST /opencode-quota-router.json` (pool and routing; actions below).
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The package ships its own `cordis.patch.yml`: it declares the `opencode-go` / `opencode-free` provid

ers and a
**single** insert (`id: opencode-router`). The `usage:` and `router:` sub-objects hold eac

h half's settings (both
halves own a `path`, so they cannot share one flat namespace).
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Top-level keys apply to both halves (`usageUrl`, `apiKeyRef`, `probeIntervalMs`, …); keys inside a s

ub-object only
override that half.
### DSH compatibility
- **dsh >= 0.2.0-rc.1** — every streaming call is routed through the public `llm/stream` waterfall.
- **dsh >= 0.2.2-rc.1** — routing additionally aligns the Session's recorded model selection before

each step
(`agent.model.select()`), so the durable request header and assistant source follow the ch

osen side.
- Older builds skip the alignment automatically; there is no version switch or extra conf
- Older builds skip the alignment automatically; there is no version switch or extra configuration.
## Account pool and failover
Pool order is usage order. Exactly one account is "current" at any time, and its key is mirrored int

o the credential
reference the provider reads (default `OPENCODE_API_KEY`). Switching accounts there

fore needs no provider config
change: `resolveApiKey` runs on every streaming call, after the `llm/s
tream` router selects the account.
- **A runs dry, B takes over**: on `QUOTA` / `ACCOUNT_QUOTA` / 429 once the official allowance is co

nfirmed spent, or
on an auth-class error (`AUTH`, `INVALID_CREDENTIAL`, `MISSING_CREDENTIAL`, `ACCOU

NT_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED`,
`CLIENT_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`), the current account is marked unusable (until the

window resets, or for 30 minutes on
auth failure), routing moves to the next enabled account and **r

etries the same step** — the turn is never downgraded.
- **Single-model quarantine**: when only one

model is out of allowance and the pool still has budget, only that model
is quarantined (30 minutes

by default); every other model keeps using the plan.
- **Whole pool dry**: only then does the route

fall back to its `fallback` (DeepSeek account by default), with a
zero-token `GET /inference/go/v1/u

sage` probe every 30 minutes (or at the rolling window reset) that returns to the
plan automatically

.
- **Upstream capacity/overload**: with `router.fallbackOnCapacity: true`, a 429 whose message matc

hes
`overloaded` / `at capacity` / `prefill_cap_refused` / `ttft_admission_refused` falls back to th

e official
subscription even while the allowance is intact. The first probe after that fallback runs

after
`router.capacityFallbackDelayMs` (60 s), because a capacity refusal clears in seconds to minu

tes. The Settings page
has a **Switch to the official subscription / Switch back to OpenCode** butto

n; the same actions are available as
`POST /opencode-quota-router.json {"action":"fallback"}` and `{

"action":"primary"}`.
- **A failure mid-step does not lose the step**: the retry happens inside the

same `llm/stream` call, so only a
primary attempt that has not produced a single chunk is rerouted.

## Official status (status.opencode.ai)
OpenCode publishes the same verdict its status page shows as JSON: `GET https://status.opencode.ai/a

pi/status`,
no authentication, refreshed about once a minute. It carries the overall verdict, one ro

w per plan (Console, logs,
inference, Go, pay-as-you-go, free inference), one row per model with the

**reason** and the live speed, and every
incident with its start time. The plugin reads it directly

(Host side, cached for `router.statusRefreshMs`, 60 s
by default) and puts it beside the local prob

e in **one** upstream status card — probe on the left, published verdict
on the right, one refresh b

utton in the head. The two cards of the previous version covered the same ground and are now
merged:

- **The verdict chip** — 正常 / 降级 / 中断 / 维护 — with a tooltip that says what it means *for you*: an
`u
pstream` reason reads *"the upstream provider is degraded — not your key and not your allowance, swi

tch to the
official subscription and keep working"*, because that is the actionable form of a Degrad

ed badge.
- **One row per model**: each route's primary model is listed once. The bare chip is what

the local probe saw (classified
code, failure count, HTTP status, quarantined until), and an 「官方 …」

chip right after it is what the published feed
says about the same model, followed by OpenCode's own

first-token latency and throughput. The previous version had a
local list *and* a published list sa

ying the same thing twice; a model the feed does not list still says so.
- **Explanations only when

something is wrong**: while the probe is green and the feed is normal, the "everything is
fine" sent

ence inside each half is not rendered — the chip already said it.
- **Open incidents** show up only

when there are some; an empty list is silence, not a row of filler.
- **刷新官方状态** re-reads the feed (

and the local probe) on demand; the page also re-reads it every 60 s while it
is open, so the badge

tracks the upstream instead of the last page load.
